metaDescription: Six wireless doorbell kits with extra receivers or buttons compared, covering range, chimes, volume and which one fits two doors or two floors.
introParagraphs: Moving up a step from the simplest doorbells mostly buys you coverage: a second receiver for another floor, a second button for a back door, or a stronger range figure for a long garden. These kits are still plug-and-play, with no wiring and no app.

We evaluated each kit from its listing and specs, comparing the number of buttons and receivers, stated range, chime and melody counts, volume ceilings and battery arrangements. This page favours the fuller kits, so most picks include at least two of something, whether receivers or push buttons.

Before you buy, decide what you actually need to cover. A flat with one door wants a different kit from a house with a front and a side entrance, and a home with a long driveway cares more about range than about melody choice. The pick notes and tables below map each kit to those situations.

products.name: SECRUI Wireless Doorbell with 2 Plug-In Receivers
products.description:
SECRUI supplies two plug-in receivers with a push button that has a colorful LED flash. The listing states a volume range from 0 to 120dB with a mute mode, 58 melodies and a memory function, plus a 300 metre wireless range. The receivers arrive paired, and different transmitters can be set to different tunes.

The second receiver makes it a good pick for a two-level home, and the memory function remembers your chosen tune and volume after a power cut. Expandability is a quiet strength, because extra buttons can be given their own tune, so you can tell the front door from the side gate by ear. The wide volume range is useful, though the top end is loud for a small flat.

Setup is as simple as plugging in and fixing the button. Compared with the SECRUI with two buttons, this one favours extra receivers over extra buttons, and compared with the AVANTEK it states a higher top volume. It is the strongest all-round pick here. If you rent, the stick-on button option means no holes in the frame, and if you own, screws hold better in a sunny spot where adhesive can soften. Walk to the farthest room once everything is plugged in and press the button to confirm both chimes ring together.
products.bestFor: A two-level home that wants a chime upstairs and downstairs.
pros: Two plug-in receivers cover two levels
Volume spans 0 to 120dB with mute
Memory keeps your tune after power loss
Extra buttons can have different tunes
cons: Top volume is too loud for small flats
Only one push button in the box

products.name: SECRUI Wireless Doorbell with 2 Buttons and 2 Receivers
products.description:
This SECRUI kit pairs two push buttons with two receivers, and both buttons trigger both chimes at the same time. It offers 58 chimes, five volume levels from 0 to 110dB and a stated range of more than 1000 feet in open air. The maker pitches it as a doorbell for large homes, and no extra wires or tools are needed.

The two-button layout is the draw for a house with a front and back entrance, since either press rings in both zones. The matching volume range is slightly lower than its sibling kit, and the chime count is the same. The cost is that every press rings both receivers, so you cannot tell which door was pressed unless you set different tunes.

Installation is plug-in and stick-on, then pair if needed. It gives you coverage for two doors where the first SECRUI gives you coverage for two floors, while the Philips offers two buttons with a single receiver. Choose it if you have two entrances. Give each button a little label on the back so that you remember which is which when you replace a battery, and pair both before you fix them to the wall, since a button already stuck down can be awkward to reset without peeling it off the door frame.
products.bestFor: A house with a front door and a side or back entrance.
pros: Two buttons ring two receivers at once
58 chimes with five volume levels
Stated range of over 1000 feet open-air
No wires or tools for installation
cons: Both receivers ring for either button
Volume ceiling is lower than its sibling

products.name: AVANTEK 1300ft Wireless Doorbell Kit with 2 Receivers
products.description:
AVANTEK offers the longest stated range in this group at 1300 feet, with one weatherproof button and two plug-in receivers. The listing gives 52 melodies from a 40 mm stereo speaker, five volume levels up to 115dB and an LED flash, plus a transmitter powered by a lithium battery with a stated life of up to three years. The button is rated IP55.

The long range suits a deep garden or a long drive where a receiver in the house must still hear the button. A lithium cell for the transmitter reduces the chore of battery changes. The chime library is smaller than the SECRUI's 58, and like every range figure, the 1300 feet is measured outdoors with a clear line of sight.

It is a straightforward kit to set up, and the two receivers let you split the chime between floors. Compared with the SECRUI two-receiver kit it has a higher range claim but a lower melody count, and against the GE it offers many times the stated range. Put the transmitter button where trees, parked cars or a metal gate are not directly in the signal path, and test at the far end of the drive. If the signal is marginal there, mounting the button a little higher often helps.
products.bestFor: Properties with a long drive or a deep garden between door and house.
pros: Longest stated range of 1300 feet here
Two receivers split chimes across floors
Lithium transmitter cell lasts up to 3 years
Button carries an IP55 weather rating
cons: Fewer melodies than the SECRUI kits
Range figure assumes a clear open line

products.name: Philips Wireless Doorbell Kit with 2 Push Buttons
products.description:
Philips supplies a complete kit with one plug-in receiver, two wireless push buttons with CR2032 batteries already fitted, mounting hardware and eight melodies including ding-dong, Westminster, knocks, fanfare, Mozart, good vibes, patriotic and tango. There are four volume levels, and the receiver goes into a standard grounded outlet.

The melody list is short but recognisable, and the pre-installed button batteries mean it works straight away. Two buttons let you cover a front and a back door with one chime. The trade is that you get a single receiver and fewer tunes and volume steps than the SECRUI and AVANTEK kits, and the listing says little about range.

It is the plain option for people who value a familiar name and a short set of tunes. Compared with the GE it uses a plug-in receiver rather than a battery one, and compared with the SECRUI two-button kit it has fewer melodies and one receiver. Because the receiver needs a grounded outlet, check the spot you have in mind before you buy, and use the mounting hardware in the box if you want the buttons to stay put through a few winters of door slamming and temperature swings.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a recognised brand and a short, simple tune list.
pros: Two push buttons for two entrances
Button batteries come pre-installed
Eight familiar melodies including Westminster
Plug-in receiver needs no battery changes
cons: Listing gives no clear range figure

products.name: AIDA Lighted Waterproof Wireless Doorbell
products.description:
AIDA focuses on the outdoor button, with an IP55 waterproof rating the listing says will cope with rain, snow and strong sun. It carries a stated range of 1000 feet, 58 chimes with a mute mode, five volume levels and an LED flash. The doorbell is battery operated on the button side and plugs in at the receiver.

The weather rating gives confidence for a doorway that takes a beating from the elements, and the LED light helps in noisy rooms. Chime and volume numbers match the SECRUI, but the kit does not add a second receiver or a second button, so it covers a single door and a single spot. The range is a best-case outdoor figure.

As a result it suits an exposed porch better than a layered house. Compared with the Philips it offers many more chimes, while against the AVANTEK it has a shorter stated range and a single receiver. Check the seal around the button periodically, and wipe off dirt and cobwebs, because even a well-rated button can fail if the gap around it fills with grit. Consider a small porch light nearby so the lit button is easy to find after dark.
products.bestFor: An exposed porch or doorway that sees rain and snow.
pros: IP55 button handles rain, snow and sun
58 chimes with five volume levels
LED flash helps in noisy rooms
Mute mode silences the chime when needed
cons: One button and one receiver only
Range figure is a best-case number

products.name: GE Battery-Operated Wireless Doorbell Kit
products.description:
GE gives you a battery-operated receiver, two push buttons with CR2032 batteries and mounting hardware in one all-in-one kit. The receiver offers up to 150 feet of range, eight melodies including ding-dong, fanfare, good vibes, knocks, Mozart, patriotic and tango, and four volume options. The receiver needs three C batteries, which are not included.

A battery receiver means no socket is needed, so it can sit on a shelf or hang in a workshop. The 150 foot range is short compared with the other kits, which suits flats and small houses but not long gardens. The three C batteries are a running cost that plug-in receivers avoid.

It is a simple, no-configuration kit with a familiar name. Against the Philips it swaps the plug for batteries and states a range, and against the AVANTEK it offers a fraction of the distance. Pick it for a small home with no spare outlet. Buy alkaline C cells in a multi-pack, write the install date on the receiver with a marker, and replace them yearly or when the chime sounds weak, because a fading battery shortens the receiver's effective range long before it stops working altogether.
products.bestFor: A small home or workshop where there is no spare outlet.
pros: Receiver runs on batteries, no socket needed
Two push buttons for two entry points
Stated range of up to 150 feet
Simple setup with no configuration
cons: Short range suits only small properties
Three C batteries are not included

buyingCriteria.explanation: Decide whether you need to cover more doors or more rooms. The SECRUI with 2 Receivers and the AVANTEK add receivers, the SECRUI with 2 Buttons adds both, and the Philips and GE add a second button to a single receiver. Two buttons help a front and back door, while two receivers help a two-storey home. Match the extra piece to the problem you have.

The AVANTEK lists 1300 feet, the SECRUI kits list 300 metres or over 1000 feet, the AIDA lists 1000 feet and the GE lists up to 150 feet. These are open-air numbers. Real range inside a house is lower. Choose a long range if the receiver is far from the door, and a short one only for a flat.

The SECRUI lists up to 120dB with mute, the AVANTEK up to 115dB, and the Philips and GE offer four volume levels. Higher is not always better, because a loud top setting is startling in a small flat. Look for a mute mode and several steps. Test the volume at night, when the house is quiet and a chime sounds far louder than it does during the day. Pick a setting that you can hear from your usual spot without making the dog bark or waking a child, and use the mute option for naps and for night shifts.

The SECRUI and AIDA offer 58 chimes, the AVANTEK 52, and the Philips and GE eight. A long list helps households that want to tell doors apart by tune. A short list is easier to scroll. Decide if you value choice or simplicity.

Plug-in receivers like the SECRUI, AVANTEK and Philips never need battery changes, while the GE needs three C batteries. The AVANTEK transmitter lists a lithium cell of up to three years. Battery receivers can sit anywhere. Think about whether you have a socket where you want to hear the bell. A plug-in receiver tucked behind a sofa or a bookcase sounds muffled, so leave it in the open, and keep it away from large metal objects. A battery receiver is the better tool for a landing or a workshop wall with no power point nearby.
The AIDA and AVANTEK list IP55 for the button. The other listings give less detail. A better rating helps on an exposed doorway. Shelter the button under a canopy where you can.

howWeEvaluated.title: Coverage layout
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how each kit's buttons and receivers map onto a typical home. The SECRUI with 2 Buttons leads on two-entry coverage, while the SECRUI with 2 Receivers and the AVANTEK lead on multi-floor use. The Philips and GE cover two doors with one chime.

howWeEvaluated.title: Range and signal
howWeEvaluated.description: We read the range claims critically. The AVANTEK leads at 1300 feet, the AIDA and SECRUI claim around 1000 feet, and the GE lists 150 feet. All are best-case numbers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Alert options
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at melody counts, volume ceilings and visual alerts. The SECRUI kits lead on volume and chimes, the AIDA and AVANTEK add LED flash, and the Philips and GE are simpler. Based on specs and buyer feedback, we flagged where a loud top setting could be a problem.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power and upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared plug-in and battery receivers and transmitter battery notes. The AVANTEK's lithium cell and the Philips pre-installed batteries lead on convenience, while the GE adds running costs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value at this budget
howWeEvaluated.description: We asked what each kit adds over a one-button, one-receiver set. The lineup positions the SECRUI with 2 Receivers as the best all-rounder, the SECRUI with 2 Buttons as the best for two doors and the AVANTEK as the best for range.

faq.q: Which kit suits a house with two doors?
faq.a: The SECRUI with 2 Buttons and 2 Receivers rings both chimes from either button. The Philips and GE give two buttons with one receiver. Pick the SECRUI if you also want chimes on two floors.

faq.q: How do I tell the doors apart?
faq.a: SECRUI states that different transmitters can be set to different tunes. Pair each button to its own tune where the kit allows it. This is the easiest way to know which door rang.
No. These kits use plug-in or battery receivers and stick-on or screw-on buttons. The Philips needs a grounded outlet.
Top volume is meant for large homes, and it is startling in a small flat. The SECRUI has five levels and a mute mode. Set it lower for evenings.

faq.q: How long do the batteries last?
faq.a: The AVANTEK lists a lithium transmitter cell of up to three years, and the Philips ships with CR2032 button batteries installed. The GE receiver needs three C batteries. Keep spares for each.

faq.q: Why is range lower than advertised?
faq.a: Range numbers are open-air. Walls, metal and appliances cut them. Test before mounting and move the button if needed, holding it in position while a helper stands at the receiver. Thick masonry, foil-backed insulation and metal doors reduce range more than people expect, so a kit with a generous claim leaves you a margin when the real conditions are poor.

faq.q: Can I add another button later?
faq.a: Some kits support extra transmitters, as the SECRUI notes. Check compatibility with the maker. The kits with two buttons already cover two doors.
